active_inquiry.closure_condition: Close the inquiry when a reproducible baseline candidate has behavioral evidence decomposed by reach, first entry, longest uninterrupted hold, residual motion, branch or posture, and target geometry, and that evidence supports one actionable next intervention or establishes that no credible route toward the goal remains.
active_inquiry.goal_connection: Identifying the dominant failure mechanism is necessary to choose an intervention that can raise uninterrupted 2-second hold success toward at least 196 of 200 official episodes; reach-only or shaped-reward progress is not sufficient evidence.
active_inquiry.question: For a reproducible baseline learned policy, which mechanism most limits official complete-hold success: failure to reach a valid posture, settling and residual motion, active endpoint hold regulation, inverse-kinematic branch or joint-limit choice, or target geometry and conditioning?
active_inquiry.rationale: The campaign has no candidate, model role, or behavioral evidence, so official assessment is impossible and no-credible-route closure is unsupported. The physical model predicts coupled reach-to-hold dynamics but does not determine which failure phase dominates. A baseline behavioral decomposition will discriminate those explanations and direct the next scientific action.

request.candidates_and_roles: No candidates exist. Working, best-known, and retained model roles are all empty.
request.cumulative_resource_use: Startup session S1 completed without training or measurement operations; no candidate, evaluation panel, or other campaign resource has been produced.
request.current_goal_gap: There is no trained candidate or behavioral evidence yet, so the campaign does not know the attainable success level or whether the dominant obstacle is reaching, settling, active hold regulation, inverse-kinematic branch choice, or target geometry near joint-limit and conditioning extremes.
request.current_synthesis: The pre-campaign physical model supports a coupled-control interpretation: bounded torque at 50 Hz must first move the damped two-joint system to a valid inverse-kinematic posture and then actively cancel residual joint motion so the endpoint remains inside a 1 cm tolerance for 100 consecutive checks. The hold requirement is the most stringent part of the goal because damping alone does not guarantee endpoint regulation, and branch posture and target geometry can change dynamic authority and boundary margin. These are mechanistic expectations, not campaign evidence.
request.decision_frontier: In goal review, choose one bounded inquiry that most reduces uncertainty about the route to 98% success. The key decision is whether to begin with behavioral failure decomposition of a baseline learned policy across target geometry and hold dynamics, or whether an implementation-level obstacle is already sufficiently evident to justify changing the policy, reward, observations, or training distribution first.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 of 200 official episodes to complete an uninterrupted 2-second hold. The initial scientific direction therefore prioritizes understanding and improving the full reach-to-stabilized-hold behavior, rather than optimizing approach reward or endpoint reach in isolation.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Open a goal-linked inquiry focused on identifying the dominant failure mechanism for complete-hold success. The first evidence-producing action should establish a reproducible baseline and quantify reach, first entry, longest hold, interruptions, residual motion, branch/posture, and target-geometry dependence; use that evidence to select any subsequent scientific intervention.

request.next_direction_or_closure: Continue with I1 in its fresh inquiry session. The first evidence-producing action should establish and measure a baseline candidate under the official task semantics; do not request official assessment until an explicit best-known candidate and supporting evidence exist.

request.description: Train a reproducible PPO baseline with the current observation, reward, target curriculum, and runtime parameters; archive all checkpoint candidates for subsequent complete-hold behavioral measurement.
request.rationale: I1 has no candidate or behavioral evidence. A fresh baseline is the highest-value discriminating action because it establishes whether the current learned-control recipe can reach and sustain the official hold at all, while preserving a reproducible reference for decomposing reach time, uninterrupted hold, residual motion, branch/posture, and target geometry.

request.description: Measure the final T1 baseline candidate on the fixed research evaluation panel and record complete-hold outcomes with reach, first-entry, hold-duration, residual-motion, IK branch/posture, joint-limit, conditioning, interruption, and target-geometry diagnostics.
request.rationale: T1 training success reached 0.97 on its training stream, but that does not establish official-distribution success or identify the limiting mechanism. Evaluating the final checkpoint under the held-out research panel is the most discriminating next action for I1 because it tests complete uninterrupted hold and supplies the behavioral decomposition required to choose an intervention.

request.reason: M1 measured this reproducible baseline at 151 of 160 complete-hold successes (94.375%) on the held-out research panel, making it the strongest evidence-backed candidate currently available while remaining below the human goal.

request.candidates_and_roles: T1:checkpoint-100352 is the best-known candidate, assigned by E4, with 100,352 training steps and 0.97 training-stream success. M1 provides its held-out behavioral evidence at 94.375% (151/160). No working candidate is assigned; no separate retained scientific role is needed.
request.cumulative_resource_use: T1 used one fresh PPO training operation for 100,352 completed steps and archived 20 candidates. M1 used one 160-episode research panel at seeds 4200-4359 with evaluation schema 6. E4 assigned T1:checkpoint-100352 as best-known. No official benchmark assessment has been requested.
request.current_goal_gap: The best-known baseline is 5.625 percentage points below the 98% research target and has no evidence of official-distribution attainment. Its remaining failures are concentrated in a negative-angle, near-joint-limit posture: 6 of 9 failures never entered tolerance and 3 entered for only 1-2 checks, while all 9 had negative minimum joint-limit margins.
request.current_synthesis: T1/M1 resolve I1's dominant baseline mechanism sufficiently for an intervention: failures are not primarily generic residual-motion or active-hold regulation failures. The 9 failures occur at target angles approximately -119 to -151 degrees, all approach or cross a joint limit, and remain on the open IK branch; the three entered episodes lost the hold almost immediately. This supports the actionable hypothesis that the learned open-branch posture lacks joint-limit margin for negative-x targets. It does not yet establish whether explicit posture/limit shaping or a different branch policy is the better remedy, so the next experiment must target posture margin without changing multiple factors.
request.decision_frontier: Run one focused training intervention that makes joint-limit margin and valid posture selection consequential while preserving the complete-hold objective, then compare its candidate against T1 on shared research seeds with the same reach, hold, residual-motion, branch, posture, conditioning, and target-geometry diagnostics. Continue only if negative-angle failures and minimum joint-limit margins improve without sacrificing the rest of the distribution.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 of 200 official episodes to complete an uninterrupted 2-second hold. M1 establishes a reproducible baseline at 151 of 160 complete-hold successes (94.375%) on a held-out research panel, so the campaign is below target and must improve the identified failure mechanism before requesting official assessment.
request.next_direction_or_closure: I1 remains open. Modify the PI-owned learning implementation for a single joint-limit/posture-aware intervention, train a new candidate, and measure it in a paired comparison with T1. Do not close I1 or request official assessment until the intervention is measured against the baseline and the complete-hold success gap is resolved or a credible route is exhausted.
